questions.explanation_english: Meeting hijacking, often referred to as videoconference disruption, occurs when an unauthorized individual gains access to a private virtual meeting room to disrupt proceedings, broadcast inappropriate content, or harass participants. Administrators can prevent such intrusions by enabling waiting rooms, restricting screen-sharing privileges, enforcing meeting passwords, and avoiding public distribution of video conference access links.
